# Clavis

> Clavis is a file-encryption app for Windows 10 and 11, made by Kapil Palanivel. It encrypts files on the user's own PC with AES-256-GCM, deriving keys from the user's password with Argon2id. There is no account and no cloud: files, passwords and recovery keys are never uploaded, so only the user holds the key.

Name note: this is "Clavis" the Windows file-encryption app (Latin *clāvis*, "key"), website https://kapilpalanivel.github.io/clavis/. It is unrelated to other products or companies named Clavis.

Current version: 3.1.0, released 2026-09-30. Installer: Clavis-Setup.exe (42 MB). A portable ZIP is also available. SHA-256 checksums for both files are published on the download page.

## Key facts

- Platform: Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit. Per-user install; no administrator rights needed.
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption. Large files are processed as a stream of 64 KiB authenticated chunks, so memory use stays small. Integrity is verified on every decrypt; a tampered or corrupted file is refused.
- Keys: the password is turned into a key with Argon2id (memory-hard). Encrypted files hide their original names.
- Recovery: an optional one-time recovery key, protected with X25519 public-key cryptography, lets the user back in after forgetting the password. It is shown once; the developer cannot recover it.
- Privacy: everything runs locally. The app only goes online to check for updates; updates are signed with Ed25519 and verified before they install. The website uses cookieless, privacy-friendly analytics.
- Explorer integration: right-click a file or folder in Windows File Explorer → Clavis → Encrypt, Decrypt, Verify or Add to Watch Folder (on Windows 11 under "Show more options").
- Other features: auto-lock on system sleep and Windows lock, session timeout, best-effort secure delete, drag and drop, light and dark themes, activity history.

## Editions and price

- Clavis Free: encrypt and decrypt individual files with the full-strength encryption above, one vault, the recovery key and integrity checks. Security features are never paywalled.
- Clavis Pro: a one-time purchase of $29 (no subscription, future updates included), bought at https://kapilpalanivel.github.io/clavis/pricing.html. Adds folder and batch encryption, multiple named vaults, watch folders (automatic encryption of new files) and a key-file second factor. No account is needed: a Pro key is checked once online with the payment provider (Lemon Squeezy) when activated, after which Pro works offline.
- The Free/Pro split applies from version 3.0; earlier versions include every feature.

## Honest limitations

- Clavis is closed-source and has not been independently audited. It uses standard, public cryptography (AES-256-GCM, Argon2id, X25519, Ed25519).
- The installer is not yet signed with a code-signing certificate, so Windows SmartScreen may show "unknown publisher" until it is.
- Secure delete is best effort: SSDs, cloud-synced folders and shadow copies may keep remnants.
- If both the password and the recovery key are lost, the files cannot be recovered by anyone.
- Windows only; there are no macOS, Linux or mobile versions.
